Former Synagogue in Deidesheim

Former Synagogue · Deidesheim, Germany

The synagogue in Deidesheim was built in 1853 and inaugurated in 1854, replacing an earlier prayer room at the marketplace that had been closed as unsafe. As the small Jewish community declined through emigration, regular services became impossible by the 1920s, and the building was sold in 1936 to a local haulier who converted it into a garage and storage space. Because it was already in private, non-Jewish ownership, the building escaped destruction during the November 1938 pogrom, though ritual objects kept elsewhere were plundered. Placed under monument protection in 1987 and purchased by the town in 1992, the synagogue was restored and reopened in 2004 as the 'Kulturhaus am Schlosspark', used for concerts, readings, and exhibitions.
